csv_path\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nimport cv2\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport torch\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\nfrom mobile_sam import SamPredictor, sam_model_registry\n\n\ndef parse_args():\n    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Refine cell masks with MobileSAM.\")\n    p.add_argument(\"weights_path\", type=str, help=\"Path to MobileSAM weights (mobile_sam.pt)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"output_path\", type=str, help=\"Output folder for the new metadata csv\")\n    p.add_argument(\"rgb_path\", type=str, help=\"Path to the RGB image\")\n \"\"\"Rasterise the original annotation (rectangle or polyline).\"\"\"\n    m = np.zeros((h, w), np.uint8)\n    try:\n        xs, ys = parse_coords(row[\"coords_x\"]), parse_coords(row[\"coords_y\"])\n        pts = np.stack([xs, ys], 1).round().astype(np.int32)\n        if len(pts) >= 3:\n            cv2.fillPoly(m, [pts], 1)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n m.astype(bool)\n\n\ndef get_box(row, h, w):\n    x0, x1 = float(row[\"xmin\"]), float(row[\"xmax\"])\n    y0, y1 = float(row[\"ymin\"]), float(row[\"ymax\"])\n    x0, x1 = np.clip([x0, x1], 0, w - smooth lightly.\"\"\"\n    m = mask.astype(np.uint8)\n    if m.sum() == 0:\n        return m.astype(bool)\n    # light smoothing removes 1px spurs / diagonal-only connections\n    k = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (3, 3))\n    opened = cv2.morphologyEx(m, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, k)\n    if opened.sum() >= 0.5 * m.sum():\n        m = opened\n    n, lab, stats, _ = 0, :]\n    if len(pts) < 3:\n        return None\n    pts = np.vstack([pts, pts[:1]])  # close polyline (matches input convention)\n    return pts\n\n\ndef main():\n    args = parse_args()\n    device cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)\n    h, w = image.shape[:2]\n\n    df = pd.read_csv(args.csv_path)\n\n    sam = sam_model_registry[\"vit_t\"](checkpoint=args.weights_path)\n    sam.to(device=device)\n    sam.eval()\n    predictor = SamPredictor(sam)\n    predictor.set_image(image)\n\n    n = len(df)\n    logits_all = np.full((n, h, w), -np.inf, dtype=np.float32)\n    boxes = are logits at full resolution (return_logits=True)\n        best, best_val = None, -1e9\n        for k in range(masks.shape[0]):\n            lg = masks[k]\n            bm = lg > 0\n            if bm.sum() == 0:\n                continue\n            inter = np.logical_and(bm, prior).sum()\n            union = np.logical_or(bm, prior).sum()\n            iou = inter / max(union, 1)\n            val = float(scores[k]) + iou\n            if val > best_val:\n                best_val, best = val, lg\n        if best is None:\n            # fallback: inscribed ellipse of the box\n            best = np.full((h, w), -1.0, np.float32)\n            e = np.zeros((h, w), np.uint8)\n            cx, cy = (box[0] + box[2]) / 2, (box[1] + box[3]) / 2\n            cv2.ellipse(e, (int(round(cx)), int(round(cy))),\n                        (max(int((box[2] - box[0]) / 2), 1), max(int((box[3] - box[1]) / 2), 1)),\n                        0, 0, 360, 1, -1)\n            best[e > 0] = 1.0\n        # restrict to (slightly padded) annotation box to avoid bleeding\n        x0, y0 = int(max(box[0] - pad, 0)), int(max(box[1] - pad, 0))\n        x1, y1 = int(min(box[2] + pad, w - 1)), int(min(box[3] + pad, h - 1))\n        lim = np.full((h, w), -np.inf, np.float32)\n        lim[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1] = best[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1]\n        logits_all[i] = lim\n\n    # Resolve overlaps: each pixel goes to the mask with the highest logit.\n    owner = np.argmax(logits_all, axis=0)\n    maxlog = np.max(logits_all, axis=0)\n    owner[maxlog <= 0] = -1\n\n    final = []\n    for i in range(n):\n        m = largest_component(owner == i)\n        final.append(m)\n\n    # Cleaning can in principle only remove pixels, so masks stay disjoint.\n    # Guard against empty results: reclaim from the raw prediction/box if free.\n    occupied = np.any(final, axis=0) if n else np.zeros((h, w), bool)\n    for i in range(n):\n        if final[i].sum() < 3:\n            box = boxes[i].astype(int)\n            cand = np.zeros((h, w), bool)\n            cand[box[1]:box[3] + 1, box[0]:box[2] + 1] = True\n            cand &= ~occupied\n            cand = largest_component(cand)\n            final[i] = cand\n            occupied |= cand\n\n    out = df.copy()\n    xs_l, ys_l = [], []\n    xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax = [], [], [], []\n    types = []\n    for i in range(n):\n        pts = ymax.append(int(pts[:, 1].max()))\n        types.append(\"polyline\")\n\n    out[\"xmin\"], out[\"xmax\"], out[\"ymin\"], out[\"ymax\"] = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax\n    out[\"coords_x\"], {"type":"text","timestamp":1793306589642,"sessionID":"ses_e769b5280ffeNOmqUcIpkmfMVF","part":{"id":"prt_18966f7760019JanFyujVob6SE","sessionID":"ses_e769b5280ffeNOmqUcIpkmfMVF","messageID":"msg_18966dd41001f2BMy7pxFA0dEE","type":"text","text":"I wrote `/app/convert_masks.py`. On the demo data it produced 48 polyline masks with no overlaps. I checked the outlines drawn on the image, and they follow the nuclei well.\n\n**Usage**\n```\npython convert_masks.py <weights_path> <output_path> <rgb_path> <csv_path>\n```\n\n**How it works**\n- **Model:** it loads MobileSAM (`vit_t`) from `mobile_sam` and runs on GPU if one exists, otherwise CPU. The image is embedded once, then each row is prompted with its `xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax` box. The demo's 48 masks took about 5 seconds on CPU.\n- **Choosing a mask:** SAM returns several candidate masks per cell. The script picks the one with the best SAM score plus overlap with the original rectangle or polyline.\n- **Overlaps:** each pixel goes to the mask with the highest logit, so masks cannot overlap. SAM's output is also clipped to the annotation box plus 3 px, so it can't bleed into neighbouring cells.\n- **One contiguous mask per cell:** each mask is lightly smoothed, reduced to its largest connected component, and has its holes filled.\n- **Output:** the outer contour becomes a closed polyline. The script rewrites `xmin`, `xmax`, `ymin`, `ymax`, `coords_x` and `coords_y`, and sets `type` to `polyline`. All other columns are kept, in the same order as the input.\n- **Output location:** if `output_path` is a folder, the CSV is written there under the input CSV's filename. If it ends in `.csv`, it is written to that path directly.\n\n**What I checked on the demo**\n- **Structure:** the columns match the input, and the bounding-box columns match the polylines.\n- **Overlap:** the maximum overlap count was 1, so no pixel belongs to two masks.\n- **Contiguity:** every mask is a single connected piece.\n\n**Things to know**\n- **Fallbacks:** if SAM returns nothing for a cell, the script falls back to an ellipse inside the box. It keeps the original box only as a last resort, with a printed warning. Neither fallback triggered on the demo.\n- **Environment changes:** the sandbox was missing `mobile_sam`, `pandas`, `torchvision` and `timm`, so I pip-installed them to test. I did not touch the MobileSAM source.\n- **Weights:** I downloaded `mobile_sam.pt` to `/tmp/mobile_sam.pt`. The script takes the weights path as an argument.","time":{"start":1793306589641,"end":1793306589641}}}
